links.reason: Both turn on the eclipse: Kural 1146 திங்களைப் பாம்புகொண் டற்று for the spread of gossip, Kuruntokai 395 அரவுநுங்கு மதியினுக் கிவணோர் போலக் களையார் for the rescue the townsfolk give the moon, and the split between spectacle and rescue is real. But the pair shares an image rather than one limiting the other, and the last clause of teaches adds 'the town's eyes' that 395 never mentions; 395 has no gossip.

Both are foster-mother laments that measure the elopement by the girl's play (கழிய காவி குற்றும், புணரி ஆடியும் against பந்து, கழங்கு, 'உயங்கின்று'). The body-versus-map contrast is overstated: Akananuru 17 spends lines 10 to 22 mapping the waterless track and the dark hill, so it measures by landscape as much as Kuruntokai 144. What is left is the shared convention.

Natrinai 324 pities the mother at home (அளியள் தாயே) while the girl runs ஆடு பந்து உருட்டுநள் போல through the elephant forest; Natrinai 66 is the mother picturing the girl's eyes reddened (சிவந்து ஒளி மழுங்கி) on the dove-haunted track. The two poems truly look from opposite ends of one elopement and judge its cost differently; 'misjudges' is a little strong but follows from the two pictures.

The shared point is the man's chest (மகிழ்நன் மார்பில் துஞ்சி; நண்ணேன் பரத்தநின் மார்பு) in a marutham sulk. But teaches is false about the Kural: 1311 charges that all women feast on him with their eyes (கண்ணின் பொதுஉண்பர்), not that the rival's disordered body is read as evidence, so the couplet does not rest on Natrinai 20's convention. Neither limits the other, so qualifies does not fit.

The link rests on two shared words, தெய்வ விழவும் and விருந்து அயர்வும் in line 42 against தெய்வம் விருந்து in Kural 43. Paripadal 17 says festival and feasting pass in turn (கை ஊழ் தடுமாற்றம்) between hill, Vaiyai and Koodal; it says nothing of ancestors, kin as a duty, or self, and யாமும் எம் சுற்றமும் is a prayer, not a duty. Calling this the couplet's householder order 'lived as a civic round' stretches the hymn.

Kuruntokai 156 asks whether the Brahmin's unwritten lore has a medicine that unites the parted (பிரிந்தோர்ப் புணர்க்கும் பண்பின் மருந்தும் உண்டோ); Kural 1102 answers in the same terms that the woman herself is the medicine (தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து). The shared மருந்து and the question-and-answer fit make the pairing teach something neither verse does alone.

Lines 11 and 12 (இரப்போர்க்குக் கவிதல் அல்லதை இரைஇய மலர்பு அறியா) do set the giving and receiving hand against Kural 222's ஈதல் and கொளல. But the poem's turn is that this same hand now begs a kuvalai from the queen (ஈஎன இரப்பவும் ஒல்லாள்) and is refused, so teaches is wrong that the habit is one 'the king cannot break': the poem shows it broken. The note leaves out the turn that the poem is built on.

Both list the night road's terrors: the tiger that killed or fought a tusker (இருங்களிறு அட்ட பெருஞ்சின உழுவை; வயக் களிறு பொருத வாள் வரி உழுவை) and the snake's gem appear in both. Akananuru 72 ends in self-blame (யானே, தோழி, தவறுஉடை யேனே) and Natrinai 255 in the wish that he not come (வாரார்ஆயினோ நன்றுமன்தில்ல). One situation reaches two different conclusions, which is what makes such a link sound.

Both refuse the bard in a marutham sulk and both call someone a liar (பாணன் பொய்யன்; ஊரன்பொய்). Teaches claims the bard's credit falls with his master's 'not on its own', but Thinaimalai 131 itself faults the bard's own nature (பண்பிலாப் பாண), and Ainkurunuru 43 rates his lying above the man's. The pair shares a topic and a word.

The image is truly shared and distinctive: யாழும் குழலும் முழவும் இயைந்தன வீழும் அருவி compresses Akananuru 82's bamboo flute, waterfall drum and bee lute. Teaches goes past the Tamil, though: in Thinaimozhi 7 the orchestra is only an epithet of the lord's land and is not tied to ஊரறி கௌவை, and in Akananuru 82 'many saw him' (கண்டோர் பலர்தில்) is her disclosure, not a danger of being seen.

The link is one shared verb, தெளிப்பவும் against தெளித்தசொல். The situations differ: Ainkurunuru 21 is a marutham ooran's assurance answered by the girl's pallor, while Kural 1154 is about a lover who leaves after saying அஞ்சல். The claim that the couplet's question 'comes after a doubt the older poem places' builds a sequence that neither verse states.

Lines 197 to 199 praise கொலைகடிந்தும் with beasts crowding the meat-sellers' huts (விலைஞர்குரம்பை மாவீண்டவும்), while the same idyll fries flesh at line 177 (ஊன்பொரிக்கும் ஒலிமுன்றில்) and eats prawn and tortoise at lines 63 and 64, as the note says (checked in kg/core). Set against Kural 256's argument that buying causes killing (விலைப்பொருட்டால் ஊன்றருவா ரில்), the pair shows the couplet holding the eater answerable where the idyll did not. Assigning the ban to the ploughmen alone follows the marker's uncertain parsing, but the teaching does not depend on it.

Natrinai 287's girl counts his crossing unafraid of the crocodile (நாம முதலை நடுங்கு பகை அஞ்சான் காமம் பெருமையின் வந்த) as proof of his love; Thinaimalai 46's friend uses the circling shark (எறிமகரம் கொட்கும் இரா) to bar the night visit and point him to asking for her (தந்து ஆயல் வேண்டா). One danger on the backwater is turned to opposite ends by two speakers.

Natrinai 380 refuses the bard with the body of new motherhood (தீம் பால் பிலிற்ற, புனிறு நாறும்மே, ஒத்தனெம் அல்லேம்), and Kainnilai 48 with age (தளர் முலையாய் மூத்தமைந்தார்), each in mock humility against the man's other women. The two stages of the wife's body are a specific observation. Kainnilai 48 line 2 is unclear, but the age reading rests on line 3, not on it.

The shared word is specific: Kural 1288 addresses him as கள்வ, whose chest harms like toddy, and Kuruntokai 318 names him கள்வனும் கடவனும் புணைவனும். Only the poem joins thief to debtor (கடவன்) and raft, bound by a வஞ்சினம், so the theft becomes the ground of an obligation. That is a real limit on the couplet's sense of the word.

Paripadal 6.98 and 99 (துனி நனி கன்றிடின் காமம் கெடூஉம்) states the measure Kural 1302 gives as salt. The poem puts the counsel in the mouths of the household (இல்லவர்) and the skilled who work until the sulk is understood (வல்லவர் ஊடல் உணர்த்தர), so the social practice behind the couplet is in the Tamil.

The formula is nearly identical: நிலம் பெயரினும் நின்சொற் பெயரல் (Purananuru 3.14) and நிலம்திறம் பெயரும் காலை ஆயினும் கிளந்த சொல்நீ பொய்ப்பறியலையே (Patitruppattu 63.6 and 7), for a Pandya and a Chera. The 'lever' clause is a little loose, but the contrast holds: பெயரல் in a செவியறிவுறூஉ poem is counsel leading to the closing advice, while Kapilar states it as fact among his அறியலையே lines.

The two share only the bard's lies (பாணன் பொய்யன்; பொழெனப் பொய்கூறா தொழி). Teaches claims the wife turns her anger on the go-between 'as the safer target', but Ainkurunuru 43 speaks straight to the man (ஊர, நின்னினும்) and calls him a liar too, and Kainnilai 37 gives no motive for addressing the bard. The psychology is supplied, not read.

The tension depends on reading Ainkurunuru 426's வேந்தன் அருந்தொழில் துறந்து as the man renouncing royal service. The line can as well mean that the king's hard war is over, which fits a mullai homecoming, and the note does not say which reading it depends on. In Akananuru 214, அமரும் நம்வயினதுவே is not plainly 'the war is our duty', and the note overrides the colophon's speaker without saying so. 'A real choice staged by akam' is built on these stretched readings.

A real puram name: Akananuru 54 has தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன் பண்ணன் சிறுகுடி, and Purananuru 173 is addressed to சிறுகுடி கிழான் பண்ணன் as the 'physician of hunger'. The note says what the akam poet does with the name: Pannan's village gooseberry sweetens the simile for the wife's prattle, and the one-line epithet carries the puram reputation.

Both are Kapilar's (by colophon) and both name Malaiyan's Mullur: முரண்கொள் துப்பிற் செவ்வேன் மலையன் முள்ளூர்க் கான நாற வந்து in Kuruntokai 312, and மலயன் ... முள்ளூர் மீமிசைப் பட்ட மாரி in Purananuru 123. The patron's hill is the measure of gifts in one and the ground of a night tryst in the other, a specific puram-akam crossing.

Both use a flood of desire against shame: காமக் கடும்புனல் உய்க்கும் நாணொடு நல்லாண்மை என்னும் புணை, and நாண் as a small sand dam (ஓங்குமணற் சிறுசிறை) that gives way when the sweet flood presses (தீம்புனல் நெரிதர). The raft carried off against the dam that holds until it breaks is a true and specific difference, split by speaker as teaches says.

In Kuruntokai 151 the hen who lost her mate to a hawk cries on the hill path (கணவற் காணாது ... குறும்பல அகவும்), and the hero's verdict is that going would end youth. In Kuruntokai 154 the hen whose cock went for food calls in loneliness (புலம்பக் கூஉம்), and the heroine asks how men learn to part. One road creature serves the decision to stay and the reproach of going.

Kural 1227 makes the sickness a flower that opens at evening (மாலை மலரும்இந் நோய்); Kuruntokai 108 shows the mullai bud taking the red sky's beauty (செவ்வான் செவ்வி கொண்டன்று) as the cows turn to their calves, and the woman says உய்யேன் போல்வல். The evening-opening flower is the real ground of the couplet's conceit. 'Rests on' claims an origin, but the shared logic holds.

594 has wealth seek the man of அசைவிலா ஊக்கம், while 371 says அசைவின்மை itself comes from ஆகூழ், a fate of gain. On a reading of 371 as determinism, effort is the source of gain in one and its product in the other, which is a real tension inside the Kural, and the question it raises is the right one.
links.text_issue: kural:594 line 1 reads க்கம்: the opening ஆ of ஆக்கம் is lost.

links.reason: There is close verbal agreement: Kural 1268 வினைகலந்து வென்றீக வேந்தன் ... மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து, and Natrinai 121 எல்லி விட்டன்று வேந்து ... எல் விருந்து அயரும் மனைவி. The king's release and the evening feast are joined in both, one as a wish and one as fulfilment on the road, so teaches is accurate.

The bangle slipping from wasted shoulders (பணைநீங்கிப் பைந்தொடி சோரும்; தணியும்எள் மென்தோள் வளை) is the commonest sign of separation, so the link starts from a shared topic. The venba does frame it under துறந்தான்கொல், so the sign-as-question point is true, but it is thin.

Both have the elopement sighted by travellers (காணேம் அல்லேம், கண்டனம்; யான்கண்டேன் கண்டாளாம்), with the couple as a matched pair. Teaches says the venba drops all reason and leaves the mother only a report, but lines 1 and 2 give advice and a reason (நமர்அவர் ஆபவேல் எண்ணிய எண்ணம் எளிதரா: if they are yours, your aim will not come easy). Qualifies is also loose for a convention shared in a shortened form.
links.text_issue: thinaimalai_nootraimpathu:89 line 2 is obscure; the marker flags it.

links.reason: On a plain reading the conflict is real: வினைஇவண் முடித்தனம் ஆயின் (Akananuru 47) against எல்லா வினையுங் கிடப்ப (Kar Narpathu 24), and the note says which reading it depends on. But the venba's own colophon is வினைமுற்றிய, which reads the line as leaving the rest of the business, and the note does not face that. The tension is open to dispute, not secure.
links.text_issue: kar_narpathu:24 colophon reads தலைமகள் நெஞ்சொடு; the poem's speaker is the man, so தலைமகன் is likely; line 4 has a Project Madurai variant.

links.reason: The camp image is truly shared: rain, a camp, a king who does not sleep (கண்படை இலனே; நள்ளென் யாமத்தும் பள்ளி கொள்ளான்). In Nedunalvadai it follows the prayer இன்னே முடிகதில் அம்ம, and in Akananuru 214 it comes beside அமரும் நம்வயினதுவே and the imagined lonely evening. The different framing is specific.

Akananuru 66 has the son stop the father's wedding procession, and Ainthinai Aimpathu 26 has இவன் run after the wedding chariot and come to grief (எய்தி இடருற்ற வாறு). Two incidents with different outcomes are not incompatible claims, so the pair qualifies rather than conflicts. The reading of இவன் as the son is itself uncertain, as the note admits.

The half-line is truly shared: திண்டேர்ப் பொறையன் தொண்டி. In Akananuru 60 Thondi measures the bangle the man must not crush before marriage; in Kuruntokai 128 its ayirai is longed for by a wingless heron on the eastern sea (குணகடல், பறைதபு நாரை), a measure of distance. The two aims are in the Tamil.

The image is the same one, a hand that clears trouble without thinking: உடுக்கை இழந்தவன் கைபோல ஆங்கே இடுக்கண் களைவது and கண் உறு பூசல் கை களைந்தாங்கே, both with களை. One is applied to friendship and one to the lover returning on the counted day (எண்ணிய நாள் வரை இறவாது), so the pairing is specific.

Both address a thing of nightfall with the same question: எம்கேள்போல் வன்கண்ணதோ நின் துணை, and எம் போல ... அகன்றாரை உடையையோ to sea, anril and flute, and Kalittokai 129 even names the hour மருள் மாலை as Kural 1222 does. The device is the same, so agrees fits. The 'survival of a sung form' is a guess about history, but the compression teaches says it shows is real.

The friend's argument is in the Tamil: பொருள் தான் பழ வினை மருங்கின் பெயர்பு பெயர்பு உறையும், so leaving for wealth is futile. Kural 619 grants that fate may deny (தெய்வத்தான் ஆகா தெனினும்) and still holds that effort pays. On the reading that fate settles wealth, the two draw opposite conclusions for action, a fair tension.

Muziri, gold for pepper and விழுப்பொருள் appear in both, a real link. But in Akananuru 149 Muziri is not the measure of the wealth refused: it sits in Chezhiyan's epithet (முசிறி ஆர்ப்பெழ வளஇ) in a chain that leads to the lilies like her eyes, and the refusal is விழுப்பொருள் எளிதினிற் பெறினும் வாரேன். So 'the stock measure of the wealth a woman outweighs' fits Purananuru 343 only.

The rattling dry uzhinjil pods on the man's road are truly shared (நெற்றுவிளை உழிஞ்சில் வற்றல் ஆர்க்கும்; வாடல் உழுஞ்சில் விளைநெற்று ... ஆடுகளப் பறையின் அரிப்பன ஒலிப்ப), both in the heroine's mouth. Akananuru 45 turns the sound into the dancing-ground drum, and Kuruntokai 39 marks the road as hearsay (என்ப). The report-not-sight point is true of 39 alone, but the pair does show the fixed sign handled two ways.

Lines 109 and 110 list quarrel among the things mixed and praised (அமர் உடலும் நட்பும் தணப்பும் காமமும் கள்ளும்). They do not state Kural 1330's logic that the sulk is love's pleasure because union follows. Teaches also leans on the poem's centre, a bitter public quarrel, which lies outside the quoted span, and calls the list 'the couplet's private economy at civic scale', more than these lines show.
links.text_issue: paripadal:20 line 100 is flagged as a possibly dropped heading, and line 105 (நெடு மால் கருங்கை) is obscure.

links.reason: Kural 560's அறுதொழிலோர் are named in full in Patitruppattu 24 (ஓதல் வேட்டல் அவைபிறர்ச் செய்தல் ஈதல் ஏற்றல்), and the poem says the king walks by their word and the world by his (வழிமொழிந்து ஒழுகி ஞாலம் நின்வழி ஒழுக). The Kural makes them depend on his guarding, so the two-way relation teaches names is in the Tamil.

Both are the friend offering elopement: நும்மூர்ச் செல்கம் எழுகமோ and என் தோழியும் வருமே. Ainkurunuru 236 gives discovery as the cause (அன்னையும் அறிந்தனள் அலரும் ஆயின்று), and Akananuru 107 his repeated departures (நீசெலவு அயரக் கேட்டொறும்). Two distinct pressures toward the same step is a specific point.

It is the same working scene: ஆரைச் சாகாட்டு ஆழ்ச்சி போக்கும் உரனுடை நோன்பகட்டு அன்ன எங்கோன் (on the salt road from கழி to கல்நாடு), and அழுந்திய சாகாட்டு எவ்வந் தீர வாங்குந் தந்தை கைபூண் பகட்டின் வருந்தி. One gives the king the ox's strength and the other gives the lover its strain and hot breath, as teaches says.

The agreement is close and verbal: பெருந் தோட் குறுமகள் அல்லது மருந்து பிறிது இல்லை யான் உற்ற நோய்க்கே, and தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து. The 'lever in a negotiation' rests on the colophon's தோழி கேட்ப; the poem itself does not show the overhearing, but the colophon is the received situation and the reading is fair.

Both are செலவு அழுங்குதல். Natrinai 126 argues by value (இளமையின் சிறந்த வளமையும் இல்லை), while Natrinai 137 sets on the very road the tusker breaking the omai to ease his mate's hunger (கயந் தலை மடப் பிடி உயங்கு பசி களைஇயர் பெருங் களிறு தொலைத்த) beside the ironic praise of the heart's hardness. The two methods of dissuasion are in the Tamil.

poems.note: The venba is obscure; the hill weeping as the jasmine laughs gives no sense for the lovers that can be stated with confidence.
A crane fussing over another bird's chick while crushing the neythal suggests a mapping, but no straying is stated and there is no thurai.

iraicchi.act: the female monkeys frolic openly with their mates by day on his hill
iraicchi.sense: the creatures of his own land enjoy their mates openly in daylight while he risks the midnight path, so he should take her openly in marriage

poems.note: The carrier is a troop of females with males rather than strictly one pair; it is taken as creatures acting together with their mates.
The venba is obscure (wheel and chariot images); there is no native thing to test.
The whole venba is scene; the buffalo returning decked with flower, fish and frog invites a reading of the straying husband, but neither poem nor thurai states the situation.

iraicchi.act: the tusker comes down to the hamlet's common holding his young mate close
iraicchi.sense: the hill lord should likewise take her openly before the village, that is, marry her

ullurai.anchor: காமம் ஒழிவ தாயினும் ... எம் தொடர்புந் தேயுமோ

poems.note: Which of the pair (creeper of the house, reed outside) stands for husband and which for the other woman can be argued, but either way two correspondences hold.

iraicchi.act: the anril cries in loneliness even though its mate has come and sleeps beside it
iraicchi.sense: her grief is like the anril's, sharper than the parting warrants, so she should not lose sleep while he is bound to return
